title: Nguni stick-fighting skirmish
summary: A stick duel from the cattle pastures of southern Africa: one long stick to strike with and one to guard. Here it is a game of touches and footwork, played to a steady beat by the crowd.
howToPlay: Watch your rival's stance: it shows what he is about to try, and on harder levels he feints.
Tap the move that beats it while the marker crosses the bright zone.
Clean touches score points; a rival who is off balance leaves a touch worth four.
Win two of the three rounds, or lead by nine points to end a round early.
rules: Only touches score; the contest is played to points and balance.
The guard stick blocks a strike and answers with a counter.
Tapping again while a move is playing out only tires you.
A move answered by its counter fails and costs a little balance.
heritageNote: Stick-fighting has long been practised by herding boys and young men of the Nguni-speaking peoples of southern Africa, who carry one stick to strike with and one to defend. Bouts are held at gatherings such as weddings, under the eye of an experienced referee, and protective gear is little used, so the skill lies in timing and footwork.
